name: Can old Los Angeles homes handle curbless showers?

mainEntity.name: Can an older Los Angeles home support a curbless shower without major floor reconstruction?
mainEntity.text: Can an older Los Angeles home support a curbless shower without major floor reconstruction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Curbless showers are popular for accessibility and a high-end look, but older homes do not always have enough floor depth to install them easily. The shower floor still needs slope to drain correctly, which can require recessed framing, a lowered subfloor, or special drain assemblies. That is why curbless showers can become more expensive than expected in older Los Angeles houses, especially if there is limited room below the floor or existing damage. Before committing, ask the contractor to inspect the framing and explain whether the design can be built without creating moisture or drainage problems. If the structure does not support it, a low-threshold shower may be a more practical alternative.
acceptedAnswer.description: A curbless shower is possible in many older homes, but it usually requires enough floor depth for proper slope, drainage, and waterproofing. If the structure is tight, the contractor may need to lower the subfloor or modify framing to make it work safely.
